workflow.title: Writing a Case Note
workflow.description: How to write a complete, accurate and clear case note for every billable activity, complete it on time, correct it appropriately and use AI safely. The induction includes four short interactive walkthroughs, a practice note and a knowledge check.

items.title: Walkthrough: Case notes and billable activities
items.body:
This illustrated walkthrough explains which activities require a case note and introduces the four readers of the notes you write.

Your progress is saved if you stop part-way.

items.title: Walkthrough: Writing a complete case note
items.body: Covers the six required details, our Identity, Assessment and Plan format and a worked example, followed by exercises on placing lines under the correct heading and identifying what a note is missing.

items.title: Reference: Identity, Assessment and Plan
items.body:
Refer to this summary while you write.

**Identity**
- the type of session (for example therapy, assessment or initial consultation)
- the date
- where it was held
- who was present

**Assessment**
- your observations and findings
- any therapy activities used

**Plan**
- the next session date
- any tasks to be done before then
- the billed time breakdown, for example 50 minutes session, 10 minutes case noting, 30 minutes travel

**Every note must show:** date · participant name · location · who was present · what was done · billed time (session, case noting and travel).

items.title: Walkthrough: Timeframes and corrections
items.body: When a note must be completed, what can still be changed after it is finalised, and when a correction must be made by addendum, with scenarios to test your understanding.

sections.title: Using AI and where notes are written

items.title: Walkthrough: Using AI safely
items.body: Using AI safely: approved platforms only, with every line checked by you. Includes an exercise on identifying an AI error, and an overview of where notes are currently written.

items.title: Practical task: write a practice note
items.body:
Write a practice session note using the Identity, Assessment and Plan headings. Use a made-up client only.

Check that it includes:
- the date
- the participant name
- the location
- who was present
- what was done
- the billed time breakdown

Then consider: **could a colleague take over this client's care from this note alone?**

items.title: Knowledge check
items.body: Eight questions covering the whole induction. The pass mark is 80%, and you may retry.

questions.question: You have finished a 15-minute invoiced phone call with a participant's parent. What is required?
options: Nothing, as the call was short
A case note, because it is a billable activity
A note only if the call is longer than an hour

questions.question: What is the latest you should complete a case note after a session?
options: By the end of the month

questions.question: Which set of details must every note show?
options: Date, participant name, location, who was present, what was done, billed time
Participant name and your signature only

questions.question: You finalised a note three days ago and have found a mistake. What should you do?
options: Revert it to draft and edit it
Delete it and write a new one

questions.question: Under which heading does the billed time breakdown belong in our format?
An AI tool wrote something that did not happen, and you saved it. Who is responsible?
Which AI tools may you use to draft a note?
options: Any tool, if you remove the participant's name

questions.question: Which wording is most appropriate for a case note?
options: Sam needed one verbal prompt to hold the spoon steadily and fed himself most of the meal

items.title: Case note sign-off
items.body: Confirm that you have read this induction and understand what is expected of you when writing case notes.
items.ack_statement: I have read and understood this induction. I will write a complete and accurate case note for every billable activity, complete it within 48 hours, make any correction after that time by addendum, and use only Opal-approved AI platforms, checking every AI-drafted note myself.

walkthroughs.title: Case notes and billable activities
walkthroughs.description: Which activities require a case note, and the four readers of each note.

steps.title: Every billable activity requires a case note
steps.body:
A case note is required for every billable activity. **Without a case note, we cannot invoice.**

This walkthrough explains which activities are billable and who reads the notes you write.

steps.title: Billable activities

image.alt: Six billable activities flow into a case note, and only then into an invoice.

steps.body:
Each of the following requires a case note:
• therapy sessions
• assessment sessions
• initial consultations
• invoiced phone calls and emails
• case management
• travel time

The note must be complete for the billing to be valid.

quiz.question: You spent 30 minutes driving to a participant's home and billed it. Does that travel need a case note?
options: No, as it is only driving
Yes, travel time is a billable activity
Only if the session was cancelled
quiz.explain: Travel time is a billable activity. If it is billed, it requires a case note.

quiz.question: You sent an invoiced email to a participant's family. What is required?
options: Nothing, as the email is the record
A note only if they reply
quiz.explain: Invoiced phone calls and emails are billable activities, so each one needs a case note.

steps.title: Who reads your case notes

image.alt: Four readers around one note: auditors, colleagues, participants and families, and you.

steps.body:
Your notes are read by more people than you may expect.

**Auditors** check them against the actual activity. They must reflect what really happened.
**Colleagues** may take over the participant's care from your note. They should understand exactly what you did.
**Participants and families** may be sent a note. They should be able to see what was done and what was billed.
**You** will use your notes later to write progress reports.

steps.title: Knowledge check: handover to a colleague

quiz.question: A colleague takes over your participant's care and reads your most recent note. What do they need from it?
options: A general sense of how the session went
Exactly what you did, so they can continue the participant's care
quiz.explain: Colleagues may take over the participant's care from your note, so they must be able to understand exactly what you did.

quiz.question: Who checks your notes against the activity that actually happened?
quiz.explain: Auditors check notes against the actual activity, so every note must reflect what really happened.

steps.title: Summary: case notes and billable activities
steps.body:
**Without a case note, we cannot invoice.** Write every note with its four readers in mind.

Return to your induction to continue with the next module: writing a complete case note.

walkthroughs.title: Writing a complete case note
walkthroughs.description: The six required details, the Identity, Assessment and Plan format, a worked example and practice exercises.

steps.title: What makes a sound case note
steps.body:
A good note serves two purposes: it supports the billing, and it tells the next reader exactly what happened.

This walkthrough covers the six required details and our three headings, presents a worked example, and then asks you to apply them.

steps.title: The six required details

image.alt: Date, participant name, location, who was present, what was done, and billed time broken into session, case noting and travel.

steps.body:
Every note must show:
• the **date**
• the **participant name**
• the **location**
• **who was present**
• **what was done**
• the **billed time**, broken into session, case noting and travel

If any of these is missing, the note may not withstand billing or audit review.

steps.title: Our format: Identity, Assessment and Plan

image.alt: Three headings: Identity, Assessment and Plan, and what goes under each.

steps.body:
We currently use three headings.

**Identity** — the type of session (for example therapy, assessment or initial consultation), the date, where it was held, and who was present.

**Assessment** — your observations and findings, and any therapy activities used.

**Plan** — the next session date, any tasks to be done before then, and the billed time breakdown, for example 50 minutes session, 10 minutes case noting, 30 minutes travel.

quiz.question: “Present: Sam, Sam's mother and the therapist.” Which heading does this line belong under?
quiz.explain: Who was present belongs under Identity, together with the session type, date and location.

quiz.question: “He needed one verbal prompt to hold the spoon steadily.” Which heading does this line belong under?
quiz.explain: Your observations and findings go under Assessment.

quiz.question: “Billed: 50 minutes session, 10 minutes case noting, 30 minutes travel.” Which heading does this line belong under?
quiz.explain: The billed time breakdown belongs under Plan, together with the next session date and any tasks.

quiz.question: “Sam and his mother will practise the spoon at two meals before then.” Which heading does this line belong under?
quiz.explain: Tasks to be done before the next session go under Plan.

steps.title: Worked example (made-up client)

image.alt: A complete example note for a made-up client, Sam Example, with each must-have ticked.

steps.body:
**Identity**
Therapy session with Sam Example (made-up). 12 March. Held at Sam's home. Present: Sam, Sam's mother and the therapist.

**Assessment**
Sam practised using a built-up spoon at lunch. He needed one verbal prompt to hold it steadily. He fed himself most of the meal and said he felt "good" about it. We also worked on opening a lunch container, which was still difficult.

**Plan**
Next session 19 March. Sam and his mother will practise the spoon at two meals before then. Billed: 50 minutes session, 10 minutes case noting, 30 minutes travel.

Note that the entry is specific, factual and easy to follow.

steps.title: Knowledge check: identify the missing detail

quiz.question: “Therapy session with Sam Example. 12 March. Present: Sam and the therapist. Sam practised the built-up spoon at lunch. Next session 19 March. Billed: 50 minutes session, 10 minutes case noting, 30 minutes travel.” Which required detail is missing?
quiz.explain: The note does not state where the session was held. The location belongs under Identity.

steps.title: Language: professional and accessible
steps.body:
Use professional, clinical language that a participant or family member could also read and understand.

Write what actually happened in the session. Do not write what you assumed, or what a tool suggested.

Clear notes make progress reports much easier to write.

quiz.question: Select the line that is written as a case note should be.
options: Sam seemed off today, probably tired
Sam fed himself most of the meal and said he felt “good” about it
quiz.explain: It records what actually happened, rather than an assumption, in language a family member could understand.

steps.title: Summary: writing a complete case note
steps.body:
Every note includes the six required details, uses the three headings and is written in factual language.

The reference sheet in your induction summarises the format. Return to your induction to continue with the next module: timeframes and corrections.

walkthroughs.title: Timeframes and corrections
walkthroughs.description: When a note must be completed, and how to correct it within and after 48 hours.

steps.title: The 48-hour timeframe

image.alt: A timeline from the session: ideally within a day, no later than 48 hours.

steps.body:
Complete your note **ideally within a day, and no later than 48 hours** after the session.

This ensures details are recorded while they are fresh, so key information is not missed.

quiz.question: You complete three sessions and drive home late. You are tired and plan to write the notes in three days. What should you do?
options: Write them in three days, as notes written while tired are worse
Aim to complete them within a day, and no later than 48 hours after the sessions
Only write notes for the longest session
quiz.explain: Three days exceeds the 48-hour limit. Notes should be completed ideally within a day, and no later than 48 hours after the session.

steps.title: Changing a finalised note

image.alt: Draft, then finalised with 48 hours to edit or revert, then locked: corrections by addendum.

steps.body:
You can save a note as a draft. Once you finalise it:
• for **48 hours** you can edit it or revert it to draft
• **after 48 hours** you cannot change the note. You must add an **addendum**.

quiz.question: You finalised a note yesterday afternoon and notice a wrong date. What can you do?
options: Edit it or revert it to draft, as you are still within 48 hours
Nothing, as a finalised note can never be changed
quiz.explain: For 48 hours after you finalise, you can edit the note or revert it to draft.

quiz.question: It is four days since you finalised a note and you find a mistake. What should you do?
quiz.explain: After 48 hours the note cannot be changed, so the correction is made by addendum.

steps.title: Check before you finalise
steps.body: Check your note carefully before you finalise it. Correcting an error at this stage is far simpler than correcting it later.

steps.title: Summary: timeframes and corrections
steps.body:
**Complete notes within a day where possible, and within 48 hours at the latest.** For 48 hours after finalising, you may edit a note or revert it to draft; after that, corrections are made by addendum.

Return to your induction to continue with the next module: using AI safely.

walkthroughs.title: Using AI safely
walkthroughs.description: Approved platforms only, checking every line, and where notes are currently written.

steps.title: Using AI at Opal
steps.body:
AI is not banned at Opal, but it must be used carefully.

• Only use **Opal-approved AI platforms**. This protects client confidentiality and privacy.
• **Review and verify every AI-drafted note** before you save it.
• You remain responsible for everything in the note.

steps.title: Reviewing an AI-drafted note

image.alt: An AI-drafted note with four lines, under a magnifying glass.

steps.body:
An approved AI tool drafted this note following a session in which you worked on a built-up spoon and opening a lunch container.

Read it carefully. **One line describes something that did not happen.**

steps.title: Knowledge check: identify the inaccurate line

quiz.question: You did not do stairs in the session. Which line must you remove or correct before saving?
options: Sam practised using a built-up spoon at lunch
We worked on opening a lunch container
quiz.explain: It did not happen, so it cannot appear in the note. You are responsible for the final note.

quiz.question: Why does Opal ask you to use only Opal-approved AI platforms?
options: To protect client confidentiality and privacy
quiz.explain: Approved platforms protect client confidentiality and privacy.

steps.title: You remain responsible
steps.body:
You cannot attribute an error to AI if it records something that did not happen.

The note must always reflect your own content and the activities you actually completed.

steps.title: Where case notes are written

image.alt: Two routes into Splose: draft in the portal and transfer, or write directly in Splose.

steps.body:
We currently use **Splose** for case notes. Each billable activity is documented there.

The Opal portal is being developed as a client management system. Case noting is being piloted in it, including a mobile app with an AI tool to help prepare notes.

At present, you may either draft in the portal tools and transfer the note to Splose, or write directly in Splose. Both are accepted. This may change as the portal develops.

steps.title: Case Notes in the portal

image.alt: Two routes into Splose: draft in the portal and transfer, or write directly in Splose.

steps.body: This is the portal's **Case Notes** tab, where case noting is being piloted. You can start a case note here, then transfer it to Splose.

steps.title: Summary: using AI safely
steps.body:
Use approved platforms only and check every line. **You are responsible for the note.**

Return to your induction to complete the practice note, the knowledge check and the sign-off.

policy.name: Case Noting and Documentation Procedure (with AI Use Procedure)
policy.summary: Every billable activity needs a complete case note finished within 48 hours (ideally within a day), changed only by addendum after 48 hours, and any AI drafting must use approved platforms with full clinician review.
